chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man fasts the day about which there is doubt whether it is from the month of Ramadan, and it turns out to be so.' He said: 'It is something for which he was divinely granted success.'

key_terms.وُفِّقَ: Was granted divine success/tawfiq — the fast counts and is a blessing from God
key_terms.يَوْمَ الشَّكِّ: Day of doubt — the last day of Sha'ban when it is uncertain if Ramadan has begun

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about fasting on the day of doubt before Ramadan?
ai.summary: Mu'awiya ibn Wahb asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the case of a person who fasts on the 'day of doubt' (yawm al-shakk) — the last day of Sha'ban when there is uncertainty as to whether Ramadan has begun — and the fast turns out to count as part of Ramadan. The Imam responded that such a fast counts as a divinely granted success (tawfiq) for that person. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that fasting voluntarily on the day of doubt (with a Sha'ban intention) is permissible, and if Ramadan is confirmed, the fast is credited.
